title: Play AC Online mod API
description: Everything a mod may use. Nothing outside this file is promised. The game, the Mods tab's install check and the mod list's upload check are all tested against it. Versioning policy: https://playaconline.com/modding/reference/versioning/

policy.description: A level is read for at least 12 months after the next level ships. A deprecated name keeps working for at least two more levels and at least 90 days, whichever is later.

levels.summary: The first level. Content is textures (a file may carry a readable label before its name), lines (a messages file), shops (each by its id in the shop table, from Nook's store and the flower shop to Katrina's tent, one block shape for every shop, each block applying while its when holds), new furniture on a vanilla base with pictures of its own (an items file, renames), letter templates, calendar days and villager line pools. Scripts get sixteen events, each handed one table. They also get log, message, the game queries, a store per town with a part per player and one per browser, settings, remote calls between mods, a seeded rng and timers on the game clock. Eight commands are declared in permissions: six (cmd.send_letter, give_item, show_line, ask, take_item, take_bells) are applied at the end of a frame's update, and two (cmd.set_shop_goods, set_shop_open) are set at the call. Mods also have depends and conflicts with version ranges, and data_version with the data_migrated event. Mods can name optional_depends, and a setting can be world or client.

limits.name: lua.budget
limits.description: Instructions one mod may run per event, counting all its handlers for that event together. The main chunk gets its own count. Library work is charged too: every 64 bytes allocated, every 4 pattern-matching steps and every element a table function touches. An allocation the memory limit refuses is charged too: one instruction for every 64 bytes the script holds. Over the limit, the script stops for the session.

limits.name: lua.deadline_ms
limits.description: Wall-clock backstop on a script's main chunk, for time the instruction count cannot see: one long call into C, or a garbage collection. The instruction budget is what stops a main chunk that does too much. On a slow device it is stretched by the device's pace (lua.pace_frame_ms).

limits.name: lua.log_per_session

limits.name: lua.event_deadline_ms
limits.description: Wall-clock backstop on one event run, for time the instruction count cannot see: one long call into C, or a garbage collection. The instruction budget is what stops an event run that does too much, and it counts the same on every device. On a slow device it is stretched by the device's pace (lua.pace_frame_ms). A busy device does not stop a mod that stays inside its budget.

limits.name: lua.frame_budget_ms
limits.description: Lua time all mods together get per frame. Once it is spent, every game event without an answer waits for the next frame, and villager_talked is skipped for the rest of that frame. command_finished and question_answered always run. It never stops or strikes a mod. At least one waiting event runs each frame, so on a slow device events wait longer but still run.

limits.name: lua.slow_run_ms
limits.description: An event run longer than this is a strike. On a slow device it is stretched by the device's pace (lua.pace_frame_ms).

limits.name: lua.slow_runs
limits.description: Strikes in a row before the script is stopped ("kept the game waiting"). A run under the limit clears the strikes.

limits.name: lua.pace_frame_ms
limits.description: The game's own work per frame that counts as full speed. Mods' Lua time is left out of it. When the game's recent frames take longer (a slow phone, a busy machine), the wall-clock limits are stretched. The stretch is recent frame work divided by this, from 1 up to lua.pace_stretch_max. It applies to lua.deadline_ms, lua.event_deadline_ms and lua.slow_run_ms. The frame cap and the instruction budget are never stretched.

limits.name: lua.pace_stretch_max
limits.description: The most a slow device stretches the wall-clock limits. At this stretch an event run's backstop is 1 second and a strike is a run over 64 ms.

limits.name: lua.deferred_events
limits.description: Events waiting for a later frame. Past that, an event is dropped and logged.

manifest.name: $schema

manifest.name: schema
manifest.description: The manifest format. Always 1.

manifest.name: api
manifest.description: The mod API level the mod is made for. The game checks a mod by the rules of its own level. It runs an older level through shims while that level is supported. Use the newest level.

manifest.name: id
manifest.description: author.mod-name, in lowercase letters, digits and dashes, with one dot. The author parts playaconline, official, admin and example are reserved for the site's own mods in the mod list. The mod list also refuses an author part that passes for one of them (official-, examples, playaconline-official).

manifest.name: name
manifest.description: The name players see, 1 to 60 characters after trimming spaces. The mod list also refuses a name with a line break, another control character or a hidden text-direction character.

manifest.name: version
manifest.description: x.y.z, each part 1 to 9 digits with no leading zero. Every upload needs a version number this mod has not used yet. The number of a refused upload can be used again.

manifest.name: authors
manifest.description: 1 to 8 names, each 1 to 40 characters. The mod list also refuses a name with a line break, another control character or a hidden text-direction character.

manifest.name: description
manifest.description: Optional text of at most 500 characters. null is refused. Leave the key out instead.
manifest.example: The flower shop becomes a tea stall in the evening.

manifest.name: tags
manifest.description: Optional. The mod list's filters: at most 5 different tags from a fixed list, lower case. Players filter the mod list by them. The game never reads them. Anything else is refused (manifest-tags).

manifest.name: scope
manifest.description: client is a Just you mod, which only you see. world is a World mod, which changes what a visitor to your town would see. Only a World mod may hold a shop (content.shops) or a calendar file with a board notice. A friend visit needs the same World mods that count (see visit_scope) on both sides.

manifest.name: content
manifest.description: What the mod adds, each a path inside the mod: textures, messages, shops, items, letters, calendar and talk. Anything else is refused. textures names a folder, and every other key names one file. There are no translations: every text shows as written.

textures.description: A folder with at least one texture file.

messages.description: The messages file: one .json file of lines.

shops.description: The shops file. Needs scope world.

calendar.description: The calendar file. A board notice needs scope world.

manifest.name: scripts
manifest.description: A Lua script and the events it listens to. events may list data_migrated only with a data_version.

main.description: The script file, ending in lowercase .lua.

events.description: Every event the script handles, each once.

manifest.name: permissions
manifest.description: The commands the mod's script may queue, each once. The game refuses any command the list leaves out. The Mods tab and the moderators' review show what the list lets the mod do. take_item and take_bells let the mod ask the player for items or Bells. The game itself shows the question with the true item and amount, and nothing is taken unless the player says yes. set_shop_goods and set_shop_open change a shop for the day and need scope world. Needs scripts.

manifest.name: exports
manifest.description: A library's remote functions by name, each with a one-line description. These are what other mods may remote.call. At most 32 names, each 1 to 32 of a-z 0-9 _. Each description is 1 to 120 characters on one line. When exports is declared, the game lets remote.add offer only these names. The Mod log says when a listed name was never offered. Needs scripts.

example.count_pieces: How many workshop pieces the player bought, as a whole number.

manifest.name: assets_original
manifest.description: Must be true. It is your promise that the mod holds only work its authors made, never files taken from the game.

manifest.name: renames
manifest.description: Maps an old full item id of this mod to the full id of an item in this mod's items file. At most 64. Needs content.items. Each rename runs once per save, and mod-items.json records it. A renamed item already in a house therefore keeps working.

manifest.name: depends
manifest.description: Mods this one needs, as mod id to version range. A range is "*", or up to 4 comparisons (>= <= > < = and a version) split by one space. At most 16. This mod loads after them. It does not load when one is missing, off, out of range or not loading. The game checks again when it starts: a mod whose dependency is not loaded before it, in range, is not loaded at all.

manifest.name: optional_depends
manifest.description: Mods this one can use but does not need, as mod id to version range. Ranges are written as in depends. At most 16. This mod always loads. An optional dependency is present when it is installed, switched on, loading and inside the range. A present one loads before this mod. One that is missing, off, not loading or outside the range is absent, and nothing waits for it. A script asks with remote.version(id). remote.call to an absent one returns nil, a message and a code. It is not an error. A mod id may be in only one of depends, optional_depends and conflicts.

manifest.name: conflicts
manifest.description: Mods this one cannot run with, as mod id to version range. At most 16. A mod id may be in only one of depends, optional_depends and conflicts. This mod stays off while a matching one is on.

manifest.name: data_version
manifest.description: A whole number 1 to 1000000 for the shape of what the scripts save. When it changes, the data_migrated event runs once per town. Listing data_migrated in scripts.events needs it.

manifest.name: settings
manifest.description: At most 16 settings the player sets on the Mods tab and scripts read with settings.get. The types are bool, number (whole, with min and max), choice (2 to 16 choices) and text (max_length 1 to 200). A setting may say "scope". "world" is the default: the value is part of the town, a friend visit compares it, and a visitor lent the mod runs the host's value. "client" is the player's own: it is never compared or sent, and each player keeps theirs on a visit. Use client for a choice that only changes what its own player sees or hears.

unbuilt_keys.description: Top-level keys reserved for planned features. Each is refused, even when null, so no mod carries one a later game would start obeying.

rules.name: shops_need_world
rules.description: content.shops requires scope world.

rules.name: shop_fields
rules.description: Every shop takes the same block, and each field means the same on every shop. The shop table (files.shops.shop_table) lists the fields each shop has, and it is read from the game itself. A field a shop does not have is left out, not refused: the rest of the block applies and the mod's row in the Mods tab names the shop and the field (code shop-field-ignored). Nook's store and Able Sisters have no lines, because their keepers speak only the disc's own words.

rules.name: unknown_keys
rules.description: A key the game does not know is refused. This applies at the top of mod.json, at the top of the shops, items, letters, calendar and talk files, and in each of their entries (a shop block, a good, a "when" and its hours, an item, a letter, a calendar day, a talk pool). The messages file is the exception, because its keys are the lines. The message is <file>: unknown key "<key>", followed by (did you mean "<known>"?) when a known key is close. $schema is known wherever a file may carry it. Keys are case-sensitive.

rules.name: json_strict
rules.description: Duplicate keys and \u0000 are refused in every JSON file.

rules.name: extensions
rules.description: A mod may hold only these file types (case-insensitive).

rules.name: frame_cap
rules.description: All mods share 4 ms of Lua time a frame. Past it, every game event without an answer (day_started, item_picked_up, scene_entered and the others) waits for the next frame. Events wait in order for each mod, at most 64 at a time, and one past that is dropped. villager_talked is skipped for the rest of that frame, so the villager says their own greeting. A mod with events still waiting is not asked for a villager_talked line until they have run. The next mod is asked instead. Each mod therefore sees its own events in the order they happened. A remote.call into a mod is not one of its events. It runs at once, inside the caller's event. command_finished and question_answered wait too, but are never dropped or skipped. villager_answered runs at once: the player is waiting on it. A command queued by a command_finished handler is applied at the next frame boundary, not the one that delivered the result. data_migrated runs as a town loads, outside the limit.

rules.name: data_migrated_needs_data_version
rules.description: scripts.events may list data_migrated only with a data_version.

rules.name: depends_not_conflicts
rules.description: A mod id may be in only one of depends, optional_depends and conflicts. None of them may name the mod itself.

rules.name: settings_world_hash
rules.description: A World mod that declares world settings adds a hash of their values to its entry in the list of mods a friend visit compares. The entry gains +<sha256 of "name=value\n" per world setting, sorted>. The visit's list of mods carries that hash and the values too, so two towns on one mod with different settings are told "same mod, different settings". A setting whose scope is client is not in the hash, and its value is never in the list. A mod with only client settings adds no hash. A mod with no client setting hashes as it did before scopes existed.

rules.name: visit_scope
rules.description: Which mods a friend visit compares. A Just you mod never counts. A World mod counts if its content has textures, shops or items (visit_scope_content), if its permissions name set_shop_goods or set_shop_open (they change a shop), or if its permissions are not a list of strings. Every other World mod does not count. That covers a mod with only lines, letters, calendar days or talk pools. No command makes a mod count. send_letter, give_item, take_item and take_bells are refused on a visit, and show_line and ask show only to their own player. Only mods that count must match between the two towns. An optional dependency is a mod like any other here. When it is a World mod that counts, it is in the list, and installing it changes what a visit compares.

rules.name: visit_scope_content
rules.description: The content keys that make a World mod count for visits, whatever its permissions. They are what a visitor must draw or meet in the town.

rules.name: world_scope
rules.description: What needs scope world, because it changes the town a visitor sees: a shops file (content.shops), a calendar file with a board notice, and the permissions set_shop_goods and set_shop_open. Everything else may be client (only you see it) or world.

rules.name: load_order_last_wins
rules.description: When two mods change the same thing, the last in load order wins it whole. For a shop that is per shop id: the later mod's blocks are that shop, and the earlier mod's change to it is not used. Two mods that change different shops both apply. The earlier mod's row in the Mods tab names the shop and the mod that has it. Inside the mod that has a shop, all its blocks for it apply. For a texture, the kind of file comes first. A file for one exact palette (tex1_..._<tlut>_<fmt>) beats any mod's every-palette file (tex1_..._$_<fmt>) for the same texture, whatever the order. Between two files of the same kind, the later mod's is drawn. A mod's texture of either kind beats the HD pack's.

rules.name: load_order_first_wins
rules.description: A villager's talk has five places for a mod's words: before, hello, topic, after and conversation. Each takes one line per talk, and every line names its place. Every mod's villager_talked handler runs, in load order, and the first line a handler returns for a place takes it. A conversation takes the whole talk, so it needs every place free; once one is taken, the event stops. Lines a script did not take a place with come from talk files, which are not first-wins: every mod's fitting pools of that place are put together and one line is picked from all of them, fresh on every talk.

rules.name: dev_reload_hot
rules.description: Developer mode reloads these while you play, with no restart: the content files named here, any .lua script ("scripts") and the files under content.textures. Developer mode means a mod loaded from a folder or from playac-mod dev. Each value is a content key, or "scripts".

rules.name: dev_reload_restart
rules.description: Developer mode loads a change to these only when the game restarts: mod.json and the content files named here. mod.json is read once at start, and so is a file added or removed. Each value is "mod.json" or a content key.

rules.name: visit_lend
rules.description: Visiting with the host's mods. When every World mod of the host that counts is a reviewed version from the mod list, a visitor can load them for that visit only, after agreeing. They run with the host's world settings. Each mod's world values travel with the visit, are checked against what its mod.json allows, and are never kept on the visitor's game. A text setting the host changed from its default must pass the site's word checks (no rude words, contact details or risky phrases). If it does not, the visit is refused instead of lent. A client setting is the visitor's own. It keeps the value the visitor set on their installed copy of the mod, and it is the default when the visitor does not have the mod. Nothing is installed. The game restarts with the lent mods, and their scripts start with an empty store that is never saved. A lent mod acts only in the host's town. At home, in the restart before the trip and the one after it, its shop, Nook goods, board notices, items, renames and commands do nothing. It therefore never changes the visitor's own town or save. A mod installed from a file cannot be lent. Nothing is lent while mods are switched off for everyone. A set that would not load whole on the visitor's game, in the host's order, with the visitor's own Just you mods and under the same limits, is refused before the restart.

rules.name: city_set
rules.description: The City's own mod set is a short list chosen by the site and changed only with a release. A City mod may hold only textures and messages. It has no shops, no scripts and no permissions.

rules.name: calendar_board_world
rules.description: A calendar file with a board notice requires scope world. The board is the town's, and a visitor reads it.

rules.name: calendar_letter_once
rules.description: A calendar day's "letter" goes out once per day per town. It goes out only in the player's own town, not on a visit and not in The City. It counts against the mod's daily send_letter limit. A refusal is written to the Mod log, never to a script.

rules.name: font_characters
rules.description: The characters the game's font draws in a mod's lines (messages, talk lines, shop greetings, show_line and ask). Every printable ASCII character is drawn, except $ * ^ | \ which are each drawn as ?. The characters # + / ; are drawn by the font's own signs. [ ] { } are drawn as ( ), ` as ' and ~ as the villagers' wavy tilde. The letters and signs listed here are drawn too. Curly quotes, dashes, the ellipsis and a no-break space become their ASCII spelling. Any other character is drawn as ?. Letters and board notices take plain ASCII only. values holds the extra characters, from the font's own table.

rules.name: permissions_need_scripts
rules.description: permissions requires scripts, because only a script can use a command.

rules.name: exports_need_scripts
rules.description: exports requires scripts, because only a script offers functions.

rules.name: own_game_only
rules.description: Nothing of a mod runs outside the player's own game. At the title screen, at player select and in the intro no event fires, no timer fires, no command is applied, no calendar letter goes out and no town data is loaded, so data_migrated does not run there either. The title screen plays a demo in the player's own save with the clock set to a date in 2001. A script never sees that date. Whatever was waiting keeps waiting and carries on when play starts: a timer that came due fires then, and a command queued before a save and quit is applied then. The one part of a script that runs outside the game is its main chunk, at start, before a town loads.

rules.name: commands_between_frames
rules.description: An event handler never changes the game. Each cmd.* call queues a command. The game applies the queue at one point in each frame: at the end of the game's update, after the world moves and before that frame is drawn. It applies commands only while the player is free, which means not in a talk, menu, cutscene, door or scene change. A command's result comes back as a command_finished event to the mod that queued it.

rules.name: commands_host_only
rules.description: Every command is refused in The City. On a visit to a friend's town, send_letter, give_item, take_item and take_bells are refused, because only the town owner's game changes a town or a player's save. show_line and ask still run.

rules.name: command_items
rules.description: A letter's present and a given item follow the shop's item rules: no money, turnips, tickets, grab bags, fossils or reserve ids. give_item also takes this mod's own new item by its full id. Full pockets refuse a mod item, because a letter cannot carry its identity. A plain item comes by letter instead.

rules.name: ids_are_numbers
rules.description: In Lua an id is always a number, never a hex string. That holds for an item, a villager and a scene. JSON data files write an item as a string, "0x2800". The commands take an item as a number, as "0x2800", or as the mod's own "author.mod:thing".

rules.name: settings_scope
rules.description: A setting is world or client. A world setting is part of the town. A friend visit compares it, and a visitor lent the mod runs the host's value. A client setting is the player's own. It is never compared and never sent, and on a visit each player runs their own value. A client setting may decide only what its own player sees or hears: a line, a question, a display choice. It may not decide what the town gets or gives up. The game checks this where it can. In an event that read a client setting with settings.get, a command that changes the town is refused with the code command-client-setting. Those commands are the values of this rule. The check covers one event. A value kept in a variable, in store or in a timer's data and used in a later event is not caught, and neither is a value passed through remote.call. timer.after is not refused after a client setting was read, because a timer that only shows its player a line later is a proper use. Those cases are the modder's to avoid. Their failure is silent: the host's town gets what the host's value says, while a visitor's copy of the mod runs the visitor's value and can show a line that does not match.

rules.name: optional_depends_order
rules.description: Load order with optional dependencies. A present optional dependency loads before the mod that names it, exactly as a needed one does. An absent one changes nothing. Present means installed, switched on, loading and inside the range. A mod whose optional dependency is outside the range still loads, and that dependency counts as absent for it.

rules.name: optional_depends_cycle
rules.description: A cycle through an optional dependency never stops a mod from loading. When every mod left to place waits for another, the earliest of them in the player's order whose needed dependencies are all placed loads next. It loads before the optional dependencies it was waiting for, and they load after it. Such a dependency is still present. remote.version and remote.call work in events. Only the promise that it loads first is dropped for that one mod, so its main chunk must not count on the dependency. A cycle made only of needed dependencies is still refused.

files.name: shops
files.title: shops.json
files.description: Changes shops, each by its id: "nook", "flower", "redd" and the rest of the shop table. A shop takes one block, or a list of blocks. A block says what changes (goods, open, own_goods, prices, services, name, lines) and, with "when", when. Every field means the same on every shop. The shop table says which fields each shop has; a field a shop does not have is left out and the mod's row says so (rule shop_fields). While a block applies its goods join the shop's own, in at most half the spots of their kind (rounded up), or with "own_goods": false they are the whole stock. When several blocks apply at once their goods are sold together, and for a single value the last of them counts. The game itself, not the page or the mod list, refuses goods with no shelf model, money, turnips, tickets, grab bags, fossils and reserve ids, and raises a price below the item's buy-back to the buy-back. items.json lists what may be stocked. A good may be an item of the same mod, by its full id, at Nook's and the flower shop. Without a price a good takes the shop's own price. Shops are off in The City. When two switched-on mods change the same shop, the one later in the load order has that shop whole and the other's change to it is not used (rule load_order_last_wins). The earlier mod's row says so.

not.description: A block needs at least one field besides "when".

block.description: One change to a shop. It needs at least one field besides "when".

open.description: true: the shop is open while the block applies, also when its own hours have it shut. false: it is shut while the block applies. Leave it out for the shop's own hours.

own_goods.description: false: while the block applies the shop sells only the goods of the blocks that apply, and every spot of a kind they do not list is bare. true (the default): the goods join the shop's own, in at most half the spots of their kind, rounded up.

goods.description: The goods. Each stands in a spot of its own kind. The shop table gives each shop's most goods in a block.

item.description: The item id as a string, "0x" and 4 hex digits, or the full id of an item in this mod's items file (author.mod:thing), at Nook's and the flower shop. Each item is listed at most once in a block. Two mod items may not share a base.

price.description: The price in Bells. Leave it out for the shop's own price.

price_percent.description: While the block applies the shop asks this percent of its own price for every good with no price of its own. 100 is the game's price. Never below the buy-back.

buy_back_percent.description: While the block applies the shop pays this percent of what it would pay for what the player sells, never more than it asks for the item. Not turnips.

additionalProperties.description: The service's price in Bells, 1 to 99999.

services.description: A service's price in Bells, by the service's name in the shop table (a haircut, a design, a dream, a fortune).

name.description: The shop's name where the game shows it: the flower shop's door sign while the shop is shut. One line.

anyOf.description: 1 to 160 characters, at most 3 line breaks.

items.description: 1 to 160 characters, at most 3 line breaks.

additionalProperties.description: One line, or a list of 1 to 8 lines the keeper picks from.

lines.description: What the keeper says, by slot (the shop table lists each shop's). A slot is one line, or a list of 1 to 8 the keeper picks from each time.

when.description: When the block or the good applies: while every key here holds. Leave it out for always.

from.description: From this time, on a 24-hour clock.

to.description: Up to this time, on a 24-hour clock. It may be past midnight.

hours.description: HH:MM to HH:MM. From and to must differ.

time.description: The game's four times of day: morning 5 to 12, day 12 to 17, evening 17 to midnight, night midnight to 5.

season.description: Spring is March to May, summer June to August, fall September to November, winter December to February.

weather.description: Cherry blossom and falling leaves count as clear.

items.description: A day of the week, monday to sunday, in lowercase.

weekday.description: Only on these days of the week.

setting.description: The name of one of this mod's settings of type bool with scope world. Holds while it is on.

shops.description: The shops this file changes, by id. Each takes one block or a list of blocks.

shop_table.title: Nook's store
shop_table.spots: Spots by kind (furniture, stationery, clothing, carpets, wallpaper, tools, umbrellas, paint, saplings, flower bags), more in a bigger store. A new set of goods is picked each day when a block lists more than the spots.
shop_table.opens: open: true opens it when it is shut for the night, but not before its morning opening, on a renovation day or in a sale's hours. open: false shuts it.

shop_table.title: The flower shop
shop_table.spots: Six spots on the benches, one kind.
shop_table.opens: open: true opens it when the clock has it shut (2 AM to 7 AM), but not while its keeper is out on her Sunday round. open: false shuts it, with its name on the door sign.

shop_table.title: Crazy Redd
shop_table.spots: Three furniture spots, set out each time the tent is entered while he is in town.

shop_table.title: Saharah
shop_table.spots: One carpet, the one she offers for yours when the player talks to her. price_percent is her fee.

shop_table.title: The fireworks stall
shop_table.spots: Its goods for the night: fans, pinwheels and balloons, set out when the stall is set up.

shop_table.title: Able Sisters
shop_table.spots: No goods. Mabel sells one service, a design.

shop_table.title: The barber shop
shop_table.spots: No goods. Tybalt sells one service, a haircut.
shop_table.opens: open: true opens it when the clock has it shut (2 AM to 7 AM). open: false shuts it.

shop_table.title: Katrina

files.name: messages
files.title: messages file

guides.title: Lines and messages: the messages file

files.description: Lines a script or another mod can use, by key. A script reads its own with message("key") and another mod's with message("author.mod:key"). This file cannot carry a $schema key, because every key is a line. Point your editor at messages.schema.json in its settings instead.

additionalProperties.description: 1 to 400 UTF-8 bytes. Lines wrap by width, not by a count of characters. A row holds 180 pixels of the game's font, which is about 24 letters. Narrow letters like i and l take less room, and wide ones like W and m take more. A page holds 4 rows.

example.gossip1: Did you hear? The museum got a new fossil!

files.name: textures
files.title: textures folder
files.description: A folder of replacement textures, named the way Dolphin names a custom texture. A mod's texture beats the HD pack. Among mods, the one lower in the list wins. The exception is that a file for one exact palette beats any mod's "$" (every palette) file for the same texture (rule load_order_last_wins). All mods' DDS textures together may take 96 MB on the graphics card, or 24 MB on a phone. Their PNGs may take 96 MB of pixels, or 24 MB on a phone. A texture past its limit is left out and named on its mod's row. A mod's texture is read a little each frame after it is first drawn, so the game's own texture shows for a moment before it. Find a texture's name in the model viewer (/viewer/).

naming.description: A palette (C4, C8) texture. <tlut> is the palette's hash.
A palette texture under any palette.
The same names as a PNG, with any case of .png. A PNG is decoded once at load and is at most 2048 a side. A DDS of the same name in the same mod is the same texture, and the first one scanned wins.

Any of these names with a label in front, so you can tell your files apart, as in bookshelf-top_tex1_32x32_626709d910129694_$_8.png. The label is 1 to 40 lowercase letters, digits and dashes, then one underscore. The game matches on the tex1_ part only. A file whose label breaks that rule is refused. Two files in one folder that are the same texture once the labels are taken off are refused when either one has a label. An item's own textures folder reads labels the same way.

files.image_formats: DDS: BC7, BC1/DXT1, BC3/DXT5 (legacy FourCC or DX10), DX10 R8G8B8A8 or B8G8R8A8, or legacy uncompressed 32 bits a pixel. 1 to 16384 a side. Level 0 only, no stored mipmaps. PNG: grey, RGB, palette, grey with alpha or RGBA, 1 to 16 bits, interlaced or not, tRNS. At most 2048 a side.

files.name: scripts
files.title: main.lua
files.description: Lua 5.4 source text, run once when the game starts. Bytecode is refused. The script registers handlers with on() and returns nothing. Each mod has its own Lua state, and mods cannot see each other's globals.
files.example: on("villager_talked", function(e) return { place = "before", line = "Hi " .. e.villager.name .. "!" } end)

files.name: items
files.title: items.json
files.description: New furniture, each on a vanilla base piece. The game also refuses a base with no model, fossils, gyroids, clothing, design pieces and pieces a player carries as an item: umbrellas, fish, bugs, tools, balloons, fans, pinwheels and diaries. In the save, a mod item is its base piece. A file beside the save (mod-items.json) maps it back. Removing the mod therefore leaves the base piece behind, and reinstalling restores the mod item. That file belongs to the save it was written beside. Next to another save of the same town, such as a backup put back or an older town file imported, it is not used. Those pieces are then plain base pieces again. An item may carry its own pictures ("textures"). They replace the base piece's textures on that item alone, in a house and on Nook's floor. On the flower shop's bench a furniture good is a leaf. Every other copy of the base keeps its look.

id.description: The item's own id. Its full id is <mod id>:<id>.

name.description: 1 to 16 characters: letters, digits, space and ' . , ! & -. It starts with a letter or digit and does not end with a space.

base.description: A south-facing furniture id: 0x1000 to 0x1FFC or 0x3000 to 0x33C4, a multiple of 4.

price.description: The price in Bells. Leave it out for the base piece's price.

textures.description: A folder inside the mod with this item's own pictures: 1 to 16 .png or .dds files named like a texture mod's files, with the base piece's texture names. Only this item draws them. The folder may not be inside content.textures or hold it.

items.description: The new items. Each one stands on a base piece of the game's own furniture.

files.name: mod-items sidecar
files.title: mod-items.json (the game's)

guides.title: New items: how it is kept

files.description: /save/card_a/mod-items.json. The game writes it beside the home save, and a mod never reads or writes it. It records which placed or carried base pieces are which mod item, and which renames have run. It rides in the cloud save and in a friend visit's town copy.

files.name: letters
files.title: letters.json
files.description: Letter templates that a mod command (send_letter) mails through the mailbox, named "<mod id>:<letter id>". The game wraps the body at the paper's width in its own font and refuses one that needs more than 6 lines. It also refuses a present that is money, turnips, a ticket, a grab bag, a fossil or not an item. Either scope.

header.description: 1 to 24 characters besides at most one {player}, where the name goes. No line break. Plain text: printable ASCII, no { or }.

body.description: 1 to 192 characters on at most 6 lines. Plain text: printable ASCII, no { or }.

footer.description: The sign-off at the foot of the letter, 1 to 32 characters. Plain text: printable ASCII, no { or }. The mailbox list shows only its first 8 characters unless the letter has a sender.

sender.description: Optional. The name in the mailbox list, 1 to 8 characters, which is all the list has room for. Without it the list shows the footer's first 8 characters, so "The Lantern Keepers" reads "The Lant". The letter itself always signs with the whole footer. Plain text: printable ASCII, no { or }.

letters.description: The letter templates. A script mails one with cmd.send_letter, and a calendar day can name one.

letters.body:
Thank you for the help.
Here is a little something.

files.name: calendar
files.title: calendar.json
files.description: Calendar days: dated days with safe effects only, and no script. A day can have a notice on the town bulletin board. The notice is posted once on the day in the player's own town, never on a visit or in The City, and needs scope world. A day can have villager lines: talk.json pools that name the day's id as their "day", in any place of the talk. A day with no notice and no letter is a date for those pools. A day can have a letter from the same mod's letters file. The letter is mailed once on the day to the player's mailbox in their own town, never on a visit or in The City, and counts against the mod's daily letter limit. A day cannot add decorations, because the game has no data format for them.

date.description: {month, day} (February 29 works) or {month, week 1 to 4 or "last", weekday 0 Sunday to 6}.

day.description: The day of the month. Not with week or weekday.

week.description: The week of the month: 1 to 4, or "last". Needs weekday.

weekday.description: 0 for Sunday to 6 for Saturday. Needs week.

board.description: A bulletin board notice: 1 to 192 characters on at most 6 lines. Plain text: printable ASCII, no { or }. Needs scope world.

letter.description: The id of a letter in this mod's letters file, mailed on the day. It is mailed once per town per day, the first time the player is free in their own town. It follows the same rules as cmd.send_letter: it goes to the mailbox or else the post office, and counts against the daily letter limit. No permission or script is needed.

days.board:
HARVEST FAIR TODAY!
Bring your best fruit.

files.name: talk
files.title: talk.json
files.description: Villager lines placed in a villager's talk. A talk is the hello, which ends in a menu (an errand, a chat, never mind); when the player chats, the game picks a topic, fresh every time: small talk (plain chat, the time of day, the weather, the month), a trade, a letter they got, a memory, a hint, or news of an event. Every pool's "place" says where its line goes; there is no default: "before" the hello (the hello and everything after it still play), as the "hello" (the menu and the topic still play; only an everyday greeting is replaced, never a hello with news such as a bee sting or a collection finished), as the "topic" (instead of the topic the game picked when it is one of the pool's "topics", small talk when it names none; the talk ends after it, as small talk does), "after" the topic (one more message before a chat ends), or the whole "conversation" (no hello, no menu, no topic: the pool's pages, then the talk ends). A line is one page or a list of pages. A special talk (a first meeting, an errand, a villager moving out, the first-job errands) never uses a pool, nor do a new player's first ten chats, whose topics are tips. For each place, the most specific pools that fit are used: this villager, else this personality, else everyone. A pool fits when its season, time, weather and calendar day, if it names them, are the ones now. Each pool that fits rolls its chance; the lines of the pools that pass are put together, from every mod, and one is picked, never the one this villager said last when there is another. When the most specific pools all roll no, that place stays the game's. A script's villager_talked line takes its place first. A pool kept to a calendar "day" speaks only on that day, in its place, like any other pool. A conversation pool is used only when no script took any place. Nothing is saved. Either scope. Pools run in The City too.

place.description: Required: where the line goes in the talk. before: ahead of the hello. hello: instead of an everyday hello. topic: instead of the topic the game picked after a chat answer. after: after the topic, before a chat ends. conversation: the whole talk.

topics.description: Only with "place": "topic": the topics the line may stand in for. Default small_talk. "any" is all six. A first-job tip, the birthday question and "should I move?" are never replaced.

villager.description: A villager's name, any case. Not with personality.

season.description: Only in this season: spring is March to May, summer June to August, fall September to November, winter December to February.

time.description: Only at this time of day, the game's own four: morning 5 to 12, day 12 to 17, evening 17 to midnight, night midnight to 5.

weather.description: Only in this weather. Cherry blossom and falling leaves count as clear.

day.description: Only on this day: the id of a day in the same mod's calendar file. This is how a calendar day gets villager lines, in any place.

chance.description: Talks in 100 where this pool's line is said, when the pool fits. Default 100: every talk it fits.

anyOf.description: A page: 1 to 160 characters, at most 3 line breaks.

items.description: A page: 1 to 160 characters, at most 3 line breaks.

anyOf.description: A line of 1 to 8 pages, each starting on a clean window.

items.description: A villager line: one page, or a list of 1 to 8 pages.

lines.description: The pool's lines. The game picks one each time.

pools.description: The pools. A pool has a place in the talk, speaks for everyone, for one personality or for one villager, and can be kept to a season, a time of day, the weather or a calendar day.

globals.name: on
globals.description: Registers a handler for an event. Call it while the mod's own script loads, not from inside a handler and not from a function another mod calls with remote.call. The event must be in mod.json's scripts.events. At most 16 handlers per event. A handler gets one table, e, holding the event's fields.

params.name: event
params.description: An event name.

params.name: fn

globals.name: log
globals.description: Writes a line to the Mods tab's Mod log and the browser console as "[Mods] <id>: ...". Arguments are joined with spaces. A line is cut at 299 bytes. At most 20 lines per event and 500 per session. A refused cmd.* or timer.* call writes a line of its own, and those lines count toward the same two limits. A script error or stop is written to the Mod log too, with a Lua traceback, whatever the limits. The log keeps the newest 400 lines of all mods. When it is full, the oldest line of the mod with the most lines goes first, so one mod cannot push out another mod's lines.

params.description: Values to print.

globals.name: message
globals.description: A line from a messages file. "key" reads this mod's own line, and "author.mod:key" reads another mod's. Returns nil when there is no such line.

params.name: key
params.description: "key" or "author.mod:key".

members.name: day_number

fields.name: mod_item

members.name: bells

members.description: The player: { name, id }, or nil before a town is loaded. A town has up to 4 residents, each playing it from their own save slot.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Stays the same for that resident in that town. It holds the resident's save slot. A new resident who later takes a freed slot can get the same id, and never gets the old resident's store.player data: the game deletes that when a resident is deleted and again when a new one is made in the slot. On a visit it is the visitor's own number, never equal to a resident's.

members.name: calendar_today
members.description: The ids of this mod's own calendar days that fall on the town's date today, in file order. Returns {} when there are none, or before a town is loaded. Only the calling mod's days are listed.

globals.name: store
globals.description: A small saved table per mod, per town. It holds strings, numbers and booleans, up to 8 KB per mod per town. It travels with the town (cloud save, backups, Export with mod data). No town is loaded while the main chunk runs, so get answers nil and set raises an error there. On a visit or in The City it lives in memory only. store.player is this player's part of it. store.client is a separate store per browser. A key cannot start with a control character (a byte under 0x20). Every store.set, store.player.set and store.client.set writes the mod's file in the save folder before it returns. The browser keeps the save folder in IndexedDB at the game's next save sync. That sync happens at a game save, and for the cloud at a mod-data upload at most every 2 minutes. A tab closed before that sync loses the last sets. Daily command counts and the rng counter are written the same way.

members.name: get
members.description: A value this mod saved in this town, or nil. It is nil while the main chunk runs. Integers come back as integers.

members.name: set
members.description: Saves a string, number or boolean under a key in this town. nil deletes the key. Keys are up to 64 bytes and strings up to 1024. A set that would take this town's store over 8 KB raises an error and changes nothing. So does a set before a town is loaded, in the main chunk.

members.name: town
members.description: Which town the store is for now, as an opaque text that changes when the town does ("v:..." away from home). nil before a town is loaded. Compare it to reload what you keep in locals when the player moves to another town.

members.name: client
members.description: The per-browser store. It has the same get, set and limits, with one store per mod per browser whatever town is loaded.

members.name: get
members.description: A value this mod saved in this browser, or nil.

members.name: set
members.description: Saves a value in this browser. nil deletes it. 8 KB per mod.

members.name: player
members.description: This player's part of the town store. It has the same get and set, per mod, per town, per player (game.player().id). It lives inside the mod's town store and shares its 8 KB. Before a town is loaded, get answers nil and set raises an error. With a town but no player in the game yet, get answers nil and set raises its own error (no player is in the game yet). When a resident is deleted, everything mods saved for them here is deleted too and its room is given back. A new resident in that save slot starts with nothing. On a visit it lives in memory only.

members.name: get
members.description: A value this mod saved for this player in this town, or nil.

members.name: set
members.description: Saves a value for this player in this town. nil deletes it. The key and value rules are the same as for store.set.

globals.name: settings
globals.description: The mod's settings from mod.json "settings", as the player set them on the Mods tab. They are read when the game starts.

members.name: get
members.description: A setting's value: the player's, else the default. It is a boolean, an integer or a string. nil for a name the mod does not declare.

globals.name: remote
globals.description: Calls between mods. One mod offers named functions and another calls them. Values are deep copies of nil, booleans, numbers, strings and tables of them, within 64 KB, 16 levels, 4096 values and 8 results. The called function runs on the caller's budget and clock, and going over stops the caller. Its commands count toward the caller's per-event limit. Its rng draws from its own counter. A call into a mod that is already running is refused.

members.name: add
members.description: Offers a function to other mods, while the script loads. Names are 1 to 32 of a-z 0-9 _, at most 32 per mod. With mod.json "exports", only the names it lists.

members.name: call
members.description: Calls a function another running mod offers. Its errors come back as yours, and it keeps running. When the mod is one of this mod's optional_depends and it is absent, nothing is called and nothing is raised: the call returns nil, a message and a code from dependency_codes.

params.description: Copied arguments.

members.name: has
members.description: Whether a running mod offers that function.

members.name: version
members.description: Whether a mod this one names in depends or optional_depends is present, and at what version. Returns its version, such as "1.2.0", when it loaded inside the range. Returns nil, a message and a code from dependency_codes when it did not. Ask in an event. In the main chunk an optional dependency that the cycle rule placed after this mod has loaded no script yet.

returns.name: version
returns.description: The version, or nil.

globals.name: cmd
globals.description: The commands. Each queues an effect that the game applies at the end of a frame's update, before the frame is drawn. Each needs its name in mod.json permissions. A call returns the command's id. When it is refused at once, it returns nil, a message and a code (command_codes). In The City every command is refused at once. On a visit send_letter, give_item, take_item and take_bells are refused at once. A command refused at once counts against no daily limit. A command queued at home and applied after the player left comes back as a failed command_finished, and its count is given back.

members.name: send_letter
members.description: Queues a letter in the player's own mailbox. The post office keeps it when the mailbox is full. The save holds an ordinary letter, so it loads without the mod.

params.name: t
params.description: { text, item?, from?, paper? } or { template }. text is 1 to 192 characters fitting 6 lines. item is a number or "0x" and four hex digits. from is 1 to 8 characters on one line ("A friend" when left out). paper is 0 to 63. template is one of this mod's own letters.json letters, by its id or "<this mod's id>:<id>". The header, body, sign-off, present and paper then all come from the template.

returns.description: The command's id. When it is refused at once: nil, then a message and a code.

more.name: message
more.description: Why it was refused, in words.

more.name: code

members.name: give_item
members.description: Queues an item into the first empty pocket. With full pockets it comes by letter. Also takes this mod's own new item by its full id (author.mod:thing). A mod item is given with its identity, as a shop sells it, and full pockets refuse it.

params.name: item
params.description: An item number, "0x" and four hex digits, this mod's "author.mod:thing", or { item, from? }.

returns.description: The command's id. When it is refused at once: nil, then a message and a code.

params.name: text
params.description: 1 to 400 bytes.

more.name: message
more.description: Why it was refused, in words.

more.name: code

members.name: ask
members.description: Queues a question with 2 to 4 answers in the player's thought window. The pick comes back as a question_answered event.

params.name: t
params.description: { text, choices }. text is 1 to 120 characters. choices is 2 to 4 answers of 1 to 16 characters.

returns.description: The command's id. When it is refused at once: nil, then a message and a code.

more.name: message
more.description: Why it was refused, in words.

more.name: code
more.description: The refusal's stable code (command_codes).

members.name: take_item
members.description: Asks the player to hand over items from their pockets. The game shows its own question, which names the item, the count and this mod. The mod's name stands between quotes, and a mod item is named as the pockets show it. A script cannot change that text. On yes the items leave the pockets and command_finished says via taken. On no, or when the window closes with no pick, nothing is taken and command_finished carries command-declined. It is refused with command-not-held when the pockets do not hold that many. Only plain pocket slots count. A wrapped present or an item held for a villager's errand is never taken. Items a command cannot give cannot be taken either (money bags, turnips, tickets, grab bags, fossils). It is refused on a visit and in The City, so a lent mod can never take anything.

params.name: t
params.description: { item, count? }. item is an item number, "0x" and four hex digits, or this mod's own "author.mod:thing". count is 1 to 15 and is 1 when left out. An item number matches plain pieces only, never a mod item standing on that piece.

returns.description: The command's id. When it is refused at once: nil, then a message and a code.

more.name: message
more.description: Why it was refused, in words.

more.name: code
more.description: The refusal's stable code (command_codes).

members.name: take_bells
members.description: Asks the player to pay Bells from their wallet. The game shows its own question, which names the amount and this mod. The mod's name stands between quotes. A script cannot change that text. On yes the Bells leave the wallet and command_finished says via taken. On no, or when the window closes with no pick, nothing is taken and command_finished carries command-declined. It is refused with command-not-held when the wallet holds less than the amount, so the wallet never goes below zero. The bank account and money bags in the pockets are never touched. It is refused on a visit and in The City, so a lent mod can never take anything.

params.name: t
params.description: { amount }. amount is a whole number of Bells, 1 to 99999.

returns.description: The command's id. When it is refused at once: nil, then a message and a code.

more.name: message
more.description: Why it was refused, in words.

more.name: code

members.name: set_shop_goods
members.description: Sets a shop's goods for the rest of the game day, as one more block after the mod's shops.json blocks for that shop. It is set at the call, with no queue, no daily cap and no command_finished, and applies from the next frame, also when the shop is shut, and is gone when the day changes or the game restarts, so set it again in day_started. nil clears it. Only for a shop with goods in the shop table, and refused when a mod later in the load order changes that shop. Needs scope world.

params.name: shop
params.description: A shop id from the shop table, like "nook" or "redd".

params.name: goods
params.description: A list of { item, price? } (item: an item number, "0x" and four hex digits, or this mod's "author.mod:thing"), as many as the shop takes in a block. Or { goods = <that list>, own_goods = false } to make them the whole stock. nil clears.

returns.name: ok
returns.description: true when it is set. When it is refused: nil, then a message and a code.

more.name: message
more.description: Why it was refused, in words.

more.name: code
more.description: The refusal's stable code (command_codes).

members.name: set_shop_open
members.description: Opens or shuts a shop for the rest of the game day, as one more block after the mod's shops.json blocks for that shop. true opens it, false shuts it, nil clears it. It is set at the call, with no queue, no daily cap and no command_finished, and applies from the next frame and is gone when the day changes or the game restarts. Only for a shop with open in the shop table, and refused when a mod later in the load order changes that shop. Needs scope world.

params.name: shop
params.description: A shop id from the shop table, like "flower" or "barber".

params.name: open
params.description: true opens it, false shuts it, nil clears.

returns.name: ok
returns.description: true when it is set. When it is refused: nil, then a message and a code.

more.name: message
more.description: Why it was refused, in words.

more.name: code

globals.name: rng
globals.description: Seeded random numbers. rng() gives a number in [0,1), rng(n) a whole number 1..n and rng(m, n) a whole number m..n. The seed is the mod, the town, the game day and how many numbers this mod has drawn in this town on this game day. Each call in a day therefore gives another number, and a reload cannot reroll. The count is saved with the town store at the end of a run that drew numbers, and a reload carries on from it. If the tab closes before that write, the same numbers come again, never new ones. A new game day starts the count at 0, and changing the game's clock gives other numbers. The count is kept in memory only away from home, for a lent mod and before a town loads. Inside a remote.call, the called mod draws from its own counter. math.random and math.randomseed are not available. Use rng().

globals.name: timer
globals.description: Timers. A script asks to be called later, and the game sends it a timer_fired event. Time is counted on the game's clock in whole game minutes, so a timer keeps counting while the game is closed and fires at the first chance after it is due. A timer never fires at the title screen or at player select. It fires once play has started (the rule own_game_only). Timers belong to the town. They are kept in this mod's town store, count toward its store.bytes and survive a save and a reload. On a visit, in The City and for a lent mod they live in memory only and are gone when the town changes. Scene changes do not touch them. A mod may have timers.per_mod waiting in one town.

members.name: after
members.description: Sets a timer that fires once, at least that many game minutes from now. It returns the timer's id. When it is refused it returns nil, a message and a code (timer_codes). Setting a timer rewrites the town store, so it is charged to the event's budget like store.set.

params.name: minutes
params.description: Game minutes to wait, 1 to 10080 (7 days).

params.name: name
params.description: What the timer is for, 1 to 40 bytes of letters, digits, _, - and . only. It comes back in timer_fired.

params.name: data
params.description: A value handed back in timer_fired. Text is up to 240 bytes with no zero byte. Empty text comes back as nil, like every empty event text.

returns.description: The timer's id, a whole number that is never reused in this town. When it is refused: nil, then a message and a code.

more.name: message
more.description: Why it was refused, in words.

more.name: code
more.description: The refusal's stable code (timer_codes).

members.name: cancel
members.description: Cancels a waiting timer of this mod in this town. It answers true when there was one. A timer that already fired, or an id from another town, answers false.

params.name: id
params.description: The id timer.after returned.

sandbox.description: Each mod runs in its own Lua 5.4 state with only these standard libraries. It takes source text only, no bytecode. The libraries are read-only. Assigning to string.<name>, rawset on a library or setmetatable on a library raises "string.<name> is read-only". getmetatable of a library or a string is the string "locked". The built-in globals (the base functions, the libraries, on, log, message, game, store) cannot be assigned, set to nil or rawset. A local may shadow one, and a mod's own globals are writable as usual. pairs(_G) lists only the mod's own globals. Work the instruction count cannot see is charged to the budget. That covers patterns (per step, and per 16 bytes of a [...] set or of a gsub replacement), comparing long strings and allocations. The run's clock is read every 100 instructions, and a run past its deadline stops. A weak-keyed table (__mode "k" without "v") keeps its keys, because weak-keyed tables made one garbage collection cost the square of their size. Weak values work as usual.

libraries.name: base
libraries.description: Lua's base functions, without the removed ones below. pcall, xpcall and setmetatable are wrapped.

libraries.name: string
libraries.description: Without string.dump. Pattern matching is charged against the budget, and string.pack, packsize and unpack per 4 bytes of their format. Read-only.

libraries.name: table
libraries.description: insert, remove, sort, concat, move and unpack are charged per element. insert, remove, sort and concat refuse a table with a __len metamethod. Read-only.

libraries.name: math
libraries.description: The math library without random and randomseed (see removed). Use rng(). Read-only.

libraries.name: utf8
libraries.description: codepoint, len and offset are charged per byte. Read-only.

libraries.name: coroutine
libraries.description: resume and close are wrapped like pcall. Read-only.

removed.name: load
removed.description: Loads code past the text-only loader.

removed.name: math.random
removed.description: Still a function, but calling it raises an error: use rng(), which is seeded so a reload cannot reroll.
removed.raises: math.random is not available: use rng() (seeded, so a reload cannot reroll)

removed.name: math.randomseed
removed.description: Still a function, but calling it raises an error: use rng(), which is seeded so a reload cannot reroll.
removed.raises: math.randomseed is not available: use rng() (seeded, so a reload cannot reroll)

wrapped.name: xpcall

wrapped.name: setmetatable

wrapped.name: string.pack
wrapped.description: Charged per 4 bytes of the format.

wrapped.name: string.packsize
wrapped.description: Charged per 4 bytes of the format.

wrapped.description: Charged per 4 bytes of the format.

events.name: villager_talked
events.description: The player starts an ordinary talk with a villager. Return where your words go in it: nil to stay quiet, a talk table { place, line, topics, ask }, or a list of talk tables, one a place. Every line names its place: a plain string is refused and logged, with nothing said. place is "before" (ahead of the hello), "hello" (instead of an everyday hello; a hello with news is kept), "topic" (instead of the topic the game picks when the player chats, if it is one of topics, small_talk when you name none, "any" for all), "after" (after the topic, before a chat ends) or "conversation" (the whole talk: no hello, no menu, no topic). line is a page of 1 to 400 bytes or a list of 1 to 8 pages. ask = { text, choices } (2 to 4 answers) goes only with "conversation": its last page asks the question, and the player's pick goes to villager_answered. Every mod's handler is called, in load order. The first line returned for a place takes it; a later one for that place is logged and not said. A conversation needs every place free and ends the event. Lines are said only when that part of the talk comes: topic and after only when the player chats. A table that is not right is logged and nothing of it is said. Special talks never reach mods. These are a first meeting, a villager moving out, one with an errand, delivery or contest going with you, a complaint, a pitfall or a bee chase, an islander, Kamakura and summer camp. No handler is called for a special talk. The villager's next ordinary talk calls it as usual, so a line a script is keeping for "the next talk" waits for that one.

events.name: day_started
events.description: A new day begins in the game. It fires once per day, also when the game starts on a new day. It does not fire again when the game restarts later on a day the town already saw, because the save holds the day it last began. If the game was not saved since that day began, the save still holds the day before, so the next start fires it again. Count days by storing the last date you saw, not by counting calls. Its handler sees the whole day, the first day of a session included: game.calendar_today() lists today's calendar days, game.town() has the date, and game.player() and store.player have the player. A command queued here is applied once the player is free in the town.

fields.name: weekday
fields.description: 0 (Sunday) to 6, as game.time().

events.name: item_picked_up
events.description: The player got an item. They picked it up, outdoors or off a room's floor, caught it with the net or the rod, or dug it up with the shovel. It fires once the item is in their pockets, or in the wallet for Bells. It does not fire for anything bought. A fish or a bug that goes into the pockets fires this event and then fish_caught or bug_caught, so a script that counts both counts that catch twice. It does not fire when the pockets were full. Outdoors the game then offers to swap the item for one in the pockets, and no event is sent whatever the player chooses. Indoors a full pocket refuses the pickup.

fields.name: item
fields.description: The item number (items.json). For a mod item, it is the base piece the item stands on.

fields.name: mod_item
fields.description: The full id ("author.mod:thing") when the pocket slot it landed in holds a mod item. That is a mod item picked up in the player's own house, the one place a mod item stands. nil for a plain item, on a visit and in The City.

events.name: scene_entered
events.description: A scene starts, such as the town, a house or a shop. Not in the title demo, at player select or in the intro (the rule own_game_only).

events.name: data_migrated
events.description: Fires once per town, when mod.json "data_version" differs from the version the town's data was written at. It runs as the town loads, before any other event's handlers run in that town. from is 0 for data from before data_version. If the handler errors, the script stops and the version stays, so the next start tries again. Migrations run in load order. A remote.call from a data_migrated handler into a mod whose own data_migrated has not run in that town yet is refused. Needs data_version.

fields.name: from
fields.description: The version the town's data was written at. 0 for data from before data_version.

fields.name: to

events.name: item_bought
events.description: The player bought a good for Bells at any counter in the game. It fires as the seller takes the price. shop says which counter: "nook" (Nook's in every size, The City's Nookington's too), "flower" (the flower shop), "redd" (Crazy Redd), "saharah" (her carpet, swapped for one of yours and Bells), "joan" (turnips), "fireworks" (the fireworks show's stall), "shrine" (the New Year fortune slip), "gyroid" (what another player put up at their gyroid) or "villager" (a villager selling you something). Test e.shop == "nook" to keep to Nook's. price is the Bells paid. ordered is true for a Nook's catalog order, which is paid now and mailed tomorrow, so it is not in the pockets yet. Only Nook's and the flower shop sell mod items. A visitor buying in a friend's town gets a plain piece, so mod_item is nil there. Paid services that hand over no good are not purchases and do not fire it. These are the barber, Katrina, the Dream Suite and an Able Sisters design.

fields.name: item
fields.description: The item number (items.json). For a mod item, it is the base piece the item stands on.

It fires once the wallet is credited. shop says to whom: "nook" (Nook's in every size, The City's Nookington's too) or "villager" (a villager buying something from your pockets). Nobody else in the game buys. item is the first good, count is how many went and bells is what they fetched. mod_item is the first good's full id when it is a mod item. What another player buys at your gyroid does not fire it. The gyroid hands you the takings later as one sum, with no record of what sold.

Only the fishing tourney makes up a length, when the fish is shown to its host. When pocketed is true, item_picked_up fired for the same catch just before this event.

events.description: A bug was netted. pocketed says whether it went into the pockets. When pocketed is true, item_picked_up fired for the same catch just before this event.

fields.description: The bug's item number (items.json). A bug is never a mod item, so this event has no mod_item.

fields.name: letter
fields.description: The letter's full id ("<mod id>:<letter id>") when it is a letter from an enabled mod's letters file, sent by cmd.send_letter{ template } or a calendar day. Nothing is written into the save for it. The game finds it by what the saved letter holds: its words (body and footer), the sender name in the mailbox list and the paper, and only among letters the game itself mailed. So it still answers after a save and a reload, and a letter a player wrote by hand with the same words is never named. nil for the game's letters, a player's letters and a cmd.send_letter{ text } letter. Two mod letters with the same words, sender and paper are told apart by nothing, and the first in load order is named. A letter mailed before its mod changed its words, sender or paper is no longer named.

events.description: A villager with no house was given one. It fires at the game start after a move-in. A brand-new town fires it for its first villagers.

events.name: timer_fired
events.description: A timer this mod set with timer.after is due. It fires once, at the end of a frame's update, in whatever scene the player is in, and the timer is gone before the handler runs. It is an event like any other. Its handlers share one instruction budget, it waits for a later frame when the frame's time is spent, and the commands it queues count against the per-event and per-day caps. At most one timer per mod fires in a frame. A timer that came due while the game was closed fires soon after the town loads. Sent only to that mod.

commands.name: take_item
commands.description: Asks the player to hand over items from their pockets. The game shows its own question, which names the item, the count and this mod. The mod's name stands between quotes, and a mod item is named as the pockets show it. A script cannot change that text. On yes the items leave the pockets and command_finished says via taken. On no, or when the window closes with no pick, nothing is taken and command_finished carries command-declined. It is refused with command-not-held when the pockets do not hold that many. Only plain pocket slots count. A wrapped present or an item held for a villager's errand is never taken. Items a command cannot give cannot be taken either (money bags, turnips, tickets, grab bags, fossils). It is refused on a visit and in The City, so a lent mod can never take anything.

params.name: t
params.description: { item, count? }. item is an item number, "0x" and four hex digits, or this mod's own "author.mod:thing". count is 1 to 15 and is 1 when left out. An item number matches plain pieces only, never a mod item standing on that piece.

returns.description: The command's id. When it is refused at once: nil, then a message and a code.

more.name: message
more.description: Why it was refused, in words.

more.name: code
more.description: The refusal's stable code (command_codes).

commands.name: take_bells
commands.description: Asks the player to pay Bells from their wallet. The game shows its own question, which names the amount and this mod. The mod's name stands between quotes. A script cannot change that text. On yes the Bells leave the wallet and command_finished says via taken. On no, or when the window closes with no pick, nothing is taken and command_finished carries command-declined. It is refused with command-not-held when the wallet holds less than the amount, so the wallet never goes below zero. The bank account and money bags in the pockets are never touched. It is refused on a visit and in The City, so a lent mod can never take anything.

params.name: t
params.description: { amount }. amount is a whole number of Bells, 1 to 99999.

returns.description: The command's id. When it is refused at once: nil, then a message and a code.

more.name: message

commands.name: set_shop_goods
commands.description: Sets a shop's goods for the rest of the game day, as one more block after the mod's shops.json blocks for that shop. It is set at the call, with no queue, no daily cap and no command_finished, and applies from the next frame, also when the shop is shut, and is gone when the day changes or the game restarts, so set it again in day_started. nil clears it. Only for a shop with goods in the shop table, and refused when a mod later in the load order changes that shop. Needs scope world.

command_codes.description: A shop command the shop cannot take: the shop is not in the shop table, it has no goods or no open, or a mod later in the load order changes that shop.
The command is not in mod.json permissions.
Wrong arguments, such as their shape, a length, the paper or the choices.
An item the command cannot hand out, or an unknown item or letter id of the mod's own. Also sent in command_finished when the mod's item or letter was gone by the time the game applied the command.
More than commands.per_event commands in one event.
The mod's queue, or the game's, is full.
The per-day limit for this command in this town is used up.
Commands are off in The City.
On a visit, only the town owner's game changes the town.
A lent mod acting outside the host's town. It arrives in command_finished, never as the return of a cmd call.
No room now. The mailbox and the post office are full, or the pockets are full for a mod item. The command still counts against the day's cap, so do not try again in a loop.
The line or question cannot be drawn in the window, because the text has too many pages. The command still counts against the day's cap.
A take the player cannot meet. The pockets do not hold that many of the item in plain slots, or the wallet holds fewer Bells.
The player said no to a take's question, or closed it with no pick. Nothing was taken.

The event read a client setting, and a client setting cannot decide what the town gets or gives up. Make the setting world, or do not read it in an event that sends a letter, gives an item, or takes an item or Bells.
